content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Fonts online

Conventional platforms like Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle offer managed services: payment processing, product hosting, and delivery in exchange for fees and platform lock-in. They handle infrastructure for you but retain ultimate control. Sovereign commerce stacks, by contrast, deploy open infrastructure on GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and Supabase. You own the code, the data, and the delivery mechanism. No platform fees. No suspensions. No geographic restrictions. The tradeoff is clear: managed convenience versus infrastructure sovereignty.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Stripe and PayPal exclude entire regions based on financial compliance or political risk. Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle inherit these restrictions because they rely on Stripe or PayPal for payments. Sovereign stacks bypass this entirely by using on-chain crypto payments via NOWPayments. No buyer account required. No KYC. Automatic webhook triggers product delivery the moment payment confirms. If your country is locked out of conventional platforms, sovereign infrastructure is not a workaround—it’s a structural alternative built at the base layer.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Conventional platforms charge 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction, plus potential suspension risks. Crypto payments via NOWPayments charge 0.5% with no monthly fees. Recommended networks like BSC, Solana, or TRON keep transaction costs under $0.10. The real cost difference is ownership: with sovereign stacks, you pay a one-time deployment fee (e.g., Edge Commerce Stack at $197) and own the infrastructure permanently. Conventional platforms charge recurring fees and retain the right to suspend your access at any time.
Stripe operates in 46 countries out of 195. Sovereign stacks work in all 195.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

On conventional platforms, your product data, customer emails, and sales history are stored on their servers. They control access. Sovereign stacks store order data in Supabase or Google Sheets, host files on Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive, and automate delivery via Cloudflare Workers. You own the database. You control the code. Automation is configured to your specifications, not the platform’s. After deployment, COREMERCH has no access—the infrastructure is yours to operate, modify, or relocate.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If your country is excluded from Stripe or PayPal, conventional platforms are not an option—they’re a non-starter. Sovereign commerce stacks are the only architecture that provides permanent payment processing, automatic delivery, and full data ownership without geographic restrictions. If you’re selling fonts, templates, or digital products in restricted regions, the choice is clear: rent temporary access from platforms that may suspend you, or deploy infrastructure you own. The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) deploys this architecture in 48 hours, fully tested and handed off to you.
